Airlocks fail slowly and silently. Check the water level every two
weeks — a dry airlock is an open door for mould and vinegar flies.

Cleaning: rinse, then a soak in hot vinegar for the stubborn film,
never soap. Soap leaves a residue that breaks surface tension and the
airlock bubbles wrong for the next month.

The three-piece airlock is the one to buy in bulk. The S-shaped glass
one looks better and clogs at the height of a violent ferment, which
is exactly when you are not watching. Replace the bung with the year,
treat it like a tyre.
